lastWeekReview.title: Crossing the River Jordan
bullets: Two million people needed to cross the flooding River Jordan — with no bridges, it would take a MIRACLE!
Joshua told the priests to carry the ARK (which stood for God) right into the water first.
The moment the priests’ feet touched the water, the river stopped and rose up in a HEAP far away.
The priests stood on DRY ground in the middle of the Jordan until all Israel had crossed over.
Twelve men took twelve STONES from the riverbed to build a memorial at Gilgal.
The miracle was a sign that our God is real, true, LIVING, and active!
lastWeekReview.discussion: Did you see God working — big or small — in your life this week? Share one thing that reminded you that God is real, and thank Him for it!
lastWeekReview.verseQuote: “He is your praise and He is your God, who has done these great and awesome things for you, which your eyes have seen.” — Deuteronomy 10:21

kidsContent.text: Israel had crossed the Jordan and was ready to fight for the good land. The first city they came to was Jericho — a STRONGLY fortified city with high, thick walls and locked gates. The king shut everyone in, sure his walls could keep Israel out.
But God’s word to Joshua was that He had already given Jericho into his hand. Then God gave VERY unusual instructions — instructions that must have seemed to make no sense at all!

For six days, the army carried the ark and marched around the city just ONCE each day. No shouting, no talking — they walked silently. Anyone watching from the wall would surely wonder, “What in the world are they doing?”

On the seventh day they marched around SEVEN times. Then the priests blew the trumpets, the captain cried “Shout!”, all the people shouted — and the wall fell flat! The city was destroyed. Only Rahab and her household were saved, just as the two spies had promised.
🌟 Who else could bring down a whole city like that? The one true and living God was with Israel — and His word is always true!

image.caption: Israel marches around Jericho and the walls fall down

kidsContent.text: Trust Even When It Doesn’t Make Sense

This whole plan sounds kind of crazy, doesn’t it? No weapons, no talking, shouting only when told! Even hearing the instructions, you might say, “That doesn’t make sense.” But Israel trusted and obeyed — and God brought the walls down.

Sometimes our parents tell us things that don’t make sense to us either. One girl’s mom told her to keep a pair of shoes by her bed at night. “Why would I need shoes in bed? That’s crazy!” she thought. But a short time later an earthquake struck, they had to run out fast — and she was SO glad her shoes were right there!

Just like Israel followed God’s instructions through Joshua, we can trust our parents’ and serving ones’ instructions, and trust what God says in the Bible. Even when something doesn’t make sense to us, God’s word is always true.
🌟 We don’t have to understand everything — we just need to trust in God and follow His word, believing it is always true and always best for us!

lesson.practicePoint: This week, when your parents or a serving one gives you an instruction — even one that doesn’t make sense to you — trust and obey right away, believing God is leading you and that His word is always true.

memoryVerse.text: Trust in Jehovah with all your heart, / And do not rely on your own understanding; / In all your ways acknowledge Him, / And He will make your paths straight.
memoryVerse.application: Sometimes God’s way doesn’t make sense to us — like marching silently around a city for seven days! And sometimes our parents’ instructions don’t make sense either. But we don’t have to lean on our own understanding. We can trust that God’s word is always true and always the very best for us.

activity.title: 📯 March Around Jericho — Trust and Obey

parts.text: Materials: A stack of cardboard boxes or blocks to build a “wall,” a “Jericho” sign, a pretend ark or box for the men to carry, and toy trumpets (or the kids’ own voices).
Setup: Build the “wall” of Jericho in the center of the room. Pick a few kids to be priests carrying the ark, a few to carry trumpets, and the rest to be the silent army of Israel.

Round 1 — Silent March: For “six days,” the whole army marches once around the wall — completely silent, no talking or shouting. The leader reminds them: we obey God’s instructions even when they seem strange!
Round 2 — The Seventh Day: March around the wall seven times. Count each lap out loud together. Everyone must stay together and stay silent until the leader gives the signal.
Round 3 — Shout! On the seventh lap, the trumpet-blowers sound their trumpets, the leader cries “Shout!”, everyone shouts — and the kids knock the “wall” down together!
📖 Connection: Israel’s marching plan didn’t make sense — but they trusted and obeyed, and the wall fell. We can trust God’s word and our parents’ instructions even when we don’t understand!

rolePlayScript.text: Scene: On top of the wall of Jericho. Two watchmen, Boaz and Hadad, peer down at the strange army circling the city below.
The city of Jericho was shut up tight — high walls, locked gates. Inside, the people watched the army of Israel do something very, very strange.
Boaz, look down there! The Israelites are marching around our city again — and they still aren’t saying a word. That’s the sixth day in a row!
No weapons, no ladders, no shouting… they just carry that golden box and walk. Once around, then they go home. What kind of army does THAT?
It makes no sense! Our walls are far too strong. Whatever they’re planning, it will never work.
Down below, Joshua speaks quietly to the army of Israel.
Stay silent, and keep marching, just as God commanded. Today we circle Jericho seven times. Trust the Lord — His word is true.
So on the seventh day the army marched around not once, but seven times. Around… and around… and around. Then the seven priests lifted their trumpets of rams’ horns.
Wait — this time they aren’t leaving! One… two… seven times around! And now — listen — the trumpets!
Now, people of Israel — SHOUT! For the Lord has given us the city!
The trumpets blast, the whole army roars, and the great wall trembles and crashes to the ground.
The wall — it’s falling! Nobody touched it! Their God is real — He fought for them!
The wall fell flat, and the city was taken. Only Rahab and her household were saved, just as the spies had promised. Israel had simply trusted and obeyed — even when the plan made no sense.
Even when we don’t understand, we will trust and obey — because God’s word is always true!

description.text: Setup: Build a tall “wall of Jericho” from cardboard boxes, foam blocks, or stacked cups in the center of the gym. All the kids line up as the army of Israel.
Rules: For six “days,” the army marches one full lap around the wall — completely SILENT. Anyone who talks or shouts too early starts that lap over.
Seventh Day: March seven laps around the wall, counting each lap together. Build the suspense — stay silent and stay together!
Shout: On the final lap, the leader yells “Shout!” — everyone shouts as loud as they can and rushes to knock the wall down together.
📖 Connection: Israel’s strange marching plan brought the wall down because they trusted and obeyed. We obey God’s word even when it doesn’t make sense!
Materials: Boxes/blocks/cups for a wall, open space
Setup: One leader stands at the far wall as the “commander.” All the kids line up at the opposite wall as the army of Israel.
Rules: This is a listening-and-obeying game. Kids may only move on the exact command the commander calls — “Silent march,” “Freeze,” “Tiptoe,” or “Shout and run!” — even if the command seems odd.
Out: Anyone who moves without a command, or does their own move instead of the one called, goes back to the start line and tries again.
Twist: The commander mixes in surprising instructions to test whether the army trusts and obeys — not just does what feels right.
📖 Connection: Israel obeyed each unusual instruction exactly. We can trust and follow God’s word and our parents’ instructions, even when we don’t fully understand!
Materials: Open space, no equipment needed
Mark a “city of Jericho” in the middle of the field — cones, a tree, or a chalk square with a “J” in the center.
Goal: The whole group circles the “city” together as the army of Israel — one silent lap for each of the first six “days.”
Rule: Stay together and stay silent. On the seventh day, circle seven times, then on the leader’s signal everyone shouts as loud as they can!
Finish: Gather in the center and thank God that He is powerful and that His word is always true, even when His way surprises us.
Materials: Just an open outdoor space with a few cones or a natural landmark for the “city”

outdoor.tip: 📯 The lesson is trust and obedience: God’s instructions to Israel made no sense, yet obeying them brought the wall down. Help the kids feel the joy of trusting and obeying — God’s word, and their parents’ instructions, are always best, even when we don’t understand.
